title: How Will Crypto Go Mainstream? Luca Netz and Brandon Millman Discuss
abstract:
PART 1 — ABSTRACT

This conversation explores the critical juncture at which crypto finds itself as mainstream adoption becomes the focus, dissecting which players—incumbents, fintech challengers, and new entrants—are best positioned to bring on-chain products and payments to the masses. The discussion matters because it highlights evolving power dynamics between infrastructure and user interfaces, stablecoin rails, and the challenges facing both startups and large institutions seeking to redefine financial activities on the blockchain. Despite progress, tensions remain around whether consumer adoption will be led by crypto-native startups or legacy fintechs, if incumbents like PayPal and Coinbase can successfully reinvent themselves, and how truly borderless and user-friendly crypto products will be before network effects or regulatory inertia set the boundaries. The conversation surfaces unresolved questions about product strategy, distribution, and the cold-start problem, making clear that both execution and timing will shape who "wins" this phase.

---

PART 2 — KEY IDEAS

- The crypto industry is transitioning from an era focused on infrastructure and speculation to one demanding real, usable products and demonstrable business models; the bar for success is rising.
- Stablecoins and user-friendly wallets are seen as foundational for mainstream adoption, with actors like Phantom lauded for reducing onboarding friction and enabling new behaviors.
- Powerful fintech incumbents such as Stripe and Robinhood are viewed as strong contenders, with Stripe’s merchant access and Robinhood's product-driven approach called out as potential game-changers.
- Middle layers (wallets/interfaces) are strategically positioned to capture the most value, as they control user experience and can quickly roll out profitable business lines atop blockchain rails.
- Incumbents like PayPal are criticized for missing key opportunities, suggesting that risk aversion and organizational inertia will hinder traditional players from leading blockchain adoption.
- Cold-start and network effects remain key barriers; successful payment and social money apps require either existing user bases or highly effective growth hacks to overcome inertia.
- Borderless, blockchain-native versions of existing fintech models are identified as a massive, largely untapped business opportunity—potentially giving rise to global, Internet-scale financial platforms for payments and remittances.
- The "everything app" thesis (one app consolidating multiple financial, social, and transactional functions) faces skepticism; panelists argue that winning in one vertical and expanding from there is a more viable approach.
- Hardware, such as crypto phones, is seen as an important but unlikely wedge for mass crypto payments; software and built-in wallet integrations remain the favored vectors.
- Regulatory, technical, and usability challenges persist, particularly regarding global on/off ramps and integrating with diverse banking systems, which may dictate the pace and shape of mainstream adoption.
